elena: Heads-up — after landing the multi-phase prefetcher (packer -> prealign -> kv-prefetch) for AWQ weight-only on staging, we see a 10-18% p95 regression on short-chat workloads. Regression started after the packer phase split landed earlier today. attaching quick notes.
matt: ack. can you paste the perf flame or the top stacks? :eyes:
elena: put a short perf snapshot below. This is a 100-concurrent short-chat run (seq_len 64). Notice the new hot path in pack_unaligned_copy and fallback_kernel_dispatch.
```
perf top -p <server_pid>
  22.4% pack_unaligned_copy
  18.1% fallback_kernel_dispatch (gptq_slow_kernel)
  12.7% kv_lookup_blocking
  9.3% prefetch_phase_sync
```
sanjay: hmm fallback_kernel_dispatch sounds like kernel chooser picking a slow path when group_size crosses a boundary. Did we change the pack alignment or group rounding in the new prealign step?
elena: yes — prealign attempts to align groups to 8 bytes for AWQ microgroups, and when input dims hit a remainder we do a per-tensor spill + call to the generic gptq kernel. That spilled case triggers the slow kernel and an extra memcpy during pack_unaligned_copy.
jia: can you share the kernel selection heuristics we used? IIRC selector prefers exact-group-fit -> low-copy, but we added a preference for minimal padding which might be causing small-group fallthrough.
elena: current heuristic (simplified):
```
if (group_size % preferred == 0) use_fast_kernel();
else if (padding_cost < threshold) use_fast_with_padding();
else use_generic_kernel();
```
The new prealign reduces padding_cost for many shapes, but for sizes that are just one element off it selects generic_kernel because prealign reports cost incorrectly (we treat element residual as high-cost).
matt: interesting. So two things: (1) generic_kernel has higher per-token latency, (2) pack_unaligned_copy adds memcpy overhead which also increases KV cache pressure (we see extra kv_lookup_blocking). So combined effect explains the p95 tail.
perf-bot: CI perf alert: p95 latency +12% on branch prefetcher-phases — see job 3376543001
elena: quick experiment results: forcing selector to prefer fast_kernel (even with small padding) removes the 12% p95 hit but increases token CPU by ~3% overall. tradeoff seems acceptable for tail-sensitive services.
sanjay: what about batching heuristics? could the prefetcher/prefetch window size be causing serialization of KV cache hits (waiting for pack to finish)?
elena: yes. We observed prefetch_phase_sync appears in the critical path when prefetch window (N=2) overlaps with pack_unaligned_copy. Increasing window to 4 amortizes pack cost across more requests and reduces p95 slightly, but increases max memory and slightly raises median.
jia: diagnostics we should run:
  - run per-kernel microbench for group sizes [1..32]
  - run kv cache telemetry w/ and w/o prealign for same request mix
  - prof stacks with inlined symbols to confirm memcpy vs compute split
matt: can you paste the microbench harness command you used? I'll run on a 4090 replicate.
elena: microbench script (run on dedicated dev machine):
```
python tools/microbench/awq_kernel_scan.py \
  --model dummy-awq-64 --group-sizes 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --iters 200 --prefetch false/true
```
Results (summary):
  group 1-3: generic_kernel latency 2.8x fast_kernel
  group 4-7: mixed, fast_kernel wins if padded to 8
  group 8+: fast_kernel consistently fastest
sanjay: ok makes sense. Action plan:
  - Fix prealign cost calc so residual=1 isn't treated as catastrophic (elena)
  - Add an override in kernel selector to prefer fast_kernel if padding < 2 elements (jia)
  - Add a metric emitting per-request "kernel_chosen" tag to console so we can correlate p95 with kernel mix (matt)
  - Experiment with increasing prefetch window to 4 on dedicated staging to validate throughput/memory tradeoffs (sanjay)
jia: small caveat — preferring fast_kernel with padding means extra zero-padding memory touches. We should make sure it won't blow up quantization dequant state caches. Add a guard to disallow on-memory-tight devices.
elena: noted. Also saw KV eviction spikes in telemetry: the memcpy case increases residency time of KV entries by ~1.2x resulting in more cache churn. I'll hook up the kv-occupancy dashboard.
matt: good. If anyone wants a quick patch I can prototype a kernel selector that scores (latency_est + padding_penalty + kv_eviction_penalty) and choose minimal score. Could run as A/B in staging.
elena: that's perfect. I'll open a short RFC/PR summarizing the microbench results + proposed selector change and tag y'all.
perf-bot: note: please attach regression trace id to the PR to help CI tie perf diffs (job 3376543001)
elena: thanks — filing now. cc @matt @sanjay @jia :thumbsup:
matt: replying with quick checklist in PR when ready.
